items.q: In August I was contacted to do a two-weeks tour with Claude Hopkins, the pianist who had been quite a popular bandleader at the Savoy and the Arcadia ballrooms.

ctx.x: In August I was contacted to do a two-weeks tour with Claude Hopkins, the pianist who had been quite a popular bandleader at the Savoy and the Arcadia ballrooms. Claude had no regular orchestra now and most of the musicians were engaged at the Rhythmn Club. Those that I remember on the tour were Ernest "Bass" Hill, Joe Jordon known as Pokey Joe on trumpet. Joe loved to play poker and that's how he became known as Pokey Joe. Joe Hayman was on alto. Also Norman Thronton and Lem Johnson was the tenor man. Lem was…

The most amusing thing about the tour was that Claude had engaged a small bus that could carry about 20 people. It was large enough for us because we were about 14 including the girl vocalist. Everytime we came to a hill that mounted for a quarter of a mile or more, the damn bus couldn't make it and we all had to go out and push it. Sometimes we had to stop pushing for ten minutes to get our breaths and Pokey Joe always had a pair of dice with him so the guys would take their minds off of pushing the bus and shot…

When the bus was rolling, there was a poker game going on until we reached our destination. We played some dates in Maryland, Delaware and Washington, D.C., where we played a river boat dance which was very agreeable at night, because the weather was about 110 in the shade during the time we were there. We stayed in D.C. for a couple of days before the tour ended. I've experienced having to push a car on different occasions on a tour, but this was the first time I helped push a bus and everyone taken it more so…
